Plot fixed-facet interval methods

Source: R/api-plotting-facet-intervals.R
plot.mfrm_facet_intervals.Rd

Plot fixed-facet interval methods

Usage

# S3 method for class 'mfrm_facet_intervals'
plot(
  x,
  comparison = TRUE,
  draw = TRUE,
  preset = "standard",
  title = paste(x$settings$facet, "estimates and contrasts"),
  subtitle = paste0(format(100 * x$settings$level, trim = TRUE),
    "% pointwise normal intervals | ", if (x$settings$method == "sandwich")
    paste0("Sandwich | ", x$settings$clusters, " independent clusters assumed") else if
(identical(x$settings$procedure, "cml_conditional_information"))
    "Conditional information" else if (identical(x$settings$uncertainty,
    "independent_anchor_delta")) "Information + anchor source" else
    "Observed information"),
  caption = if (any(!is.finite(x$table$Estimate)))
    paste0("Not estimated: no point or interval | ",
    "Crosses: estimated points with unavailable intervals") else if (any(x$table$Status
    != "available"))
    "Open diamonds: fixed targets | Crosses: unavailable selected intervals" else NULL,
  reference = 0,
  show_legend = TRUE,
  ...
)

Arguments

x

Output from mfrm_facet_intervals().

comparison

Logical. With a sandwich result, also show its ordinary model-based interval. With source-propagated anchors, show the separate conditional-on-anchors interval. Both use the same point estimate.

draw

Logical; FALSE returns exact plotted data without opening a device.

preset

A package plot preset, for example "standard" or "monochrome".

title, subtitle, caption

Optional returned text; NULL omits it. Defaults describe the facet, exact confidence level, method and fixed/unavailable symbols. This text is not drawn; use plot_data(p, "notes") and plot_data(p, "title") to retrieve it.

reference

Optional finite vertical reference; default zero. Use NULL to omit it. This is not a rater-quality threshold.

show_legend

Logical; show the method legend (default TRUE).

...

Unused.

Value

Invisibly, an mfrm_plot_data object retaining the table, contrast coefficients, settings and labels. Use plot_data() for custom graphics; as_ggplot() returns a customizable ggplot with the same saved values.

Details

Fixed targets use open diamonds without inferential intervals. A conditionally fixed anchor can have a source-propagated interval; the comparison displays its conditional fixed value separately. Method labels distinguish source propagation from conditional observed information. Unavailable intervals in either displayed method use crosses; an ordinary comparison interval does not substitute for a missing sandwich interval. The zero line is a reference, not a threshold of practical importance or a rater-quality rule. No fit or covariance is recalculated. Target order is preserved. Weak-information cautions remain in the returned data and appear in the default subtitle. Custom or omitted subtitles change display only. For experimental two-family GPCM locations, the axis uses fixed-N(0,1) ability units and the default subtitle states the location reference and unqualified coverage, with a deficient Person-score rank caution when applicable. These are not uniform expected-rating differences. Standardized contrast axes use population SD units; returned notes identify whether SD uncertainty is estimated or the known SD is one. Reviewed interaction contrasts retain group direction, panel weights and scale in their source result; returned labels distinguish them from facet locations. Native CML intervals are labeled conditional information. Their returned notes describe asymptotic validity without implying weak information or an estimated ability population SD. When a comparison has no estimate, its row is labeled "not estimated" and has no point or interval. An empty display range is only an axis placeholder; it does not assign a value to unavailable targets. Joint interaction-cell results retain cell identities, counts and sparse flags in plot_data(p, "interaction_cells"). Their axis uses additive predictor shifts; row labels show the two level names in fitted facet order. Units follow the fixed N(0,1) ability scale. Positive effects raise expected coded scores relative to the jointly fitted main effects. These pointwise intervals are not fixed-baseline bias screens or fairness labels.

Session plot defaults

Set options(mfrmr.plot_preset = "publication") to choose a session default for plotting functions that expose the common preset argument. The supported values are "standard", "publication", "compact" and "monochrome". Precedence is an explicit call argument, then the session option, then "standard". For example, preset = "standard" overrides a session set to "monochrome". Explicit preset = NULL retains the earlier package-default behavior; it does not read the session option. Invalid session values cause an error only when that option is needed.

The category-curve, data-quality, fit-review, connectivity and network routes of plot() for report bundles use the same option through .... Plots without a common preset argument, including extended-model plots with their own palette controls, keep their own settings. This option selects a preset, not a universal theme or a guarantee that all renderers implement every appearance control identically.

New plot payloads retain the resolved preset for supported saved-data rendering. Converting an existing payload with as_ggplot() uses its saved appearance, even after the session option changes. A call that creates a new plot from a fit or statistical result uses the current default. For a reproducible script, supply preset explicitly or set the option in that script. Saving only the fitted model does not save a session option. No global ggplot theme is changed.

Restore previous settings with old <- options(mfrmr.plot_preset = "monochrome") followed by options(old). Use options(mfrmr.plot_preset = NULL) to remove the option. The preset changes appearance, not estimates, confidence levels or diagnostic thresholds.
